Arthur Cassemiro · PhD thesis, Unicamp, Instituto de Economia · prepared for Vivien · 22 October 2026

There is no clean line from the Union's money to a state road. A payment leaves a state Treasury source that is in fact a loan, an earmarked fund, the counterpart of a federal transfer, or a concession fee. This document maps where the money is visible and where it is not, so that the governance parameters of the thesis can be coded on measured fields.

Every number comes from the thesis bases; nothing is typed by hand. Budget stages are never added. What cannot be measured is said, not filled. Colours are fixed throughout: one per financing channel and one per level of government.

Part 2. Federative Aspects of the States

The fiscal room of the states, which is the room their road programmes have, in three facts: transfers from the Union are a very small part of what a state receives; federal road money reaches a state's territory through DNIT, not through transfers; and the CAPAG rating is the gate to the credit that pays the large works. The series behind these facts (credit waves, debt, annual volatility) are in the appendix; Finding 2 in Part 4 draws on them.

Part 3. The Financing Channels Trajectories

The thesis follows five channels. 1a is the entity's own budget (the Union's through DNIT, the state's through its Treasury or an earmarked fund). 1b is a Union transfer to a state or municipality. 2 is a state-owned company. 3 is a domestic loan to the government (BNDES, Caixa, Banco do Brasil). 4 is an external loan (World Bank, IDB, CAF and others). 5 is private capital under a concession or PPP. Colours are fixed throughout the page.

Part 5. Conclusions: Three Answers from the Data

1. Does road investment use more than one channel for the same work?

Yes, often, and the answer depends on the unit. Charts 7 and 8 follow one work, the Rodoanel Norte, through a federal term of 1999, a Treasury that pays the expropriations, an IDB loan, a state company that holds the contracts, and a PPP: four channels and three executors, with no ledger that holds the chain. On the whole base, at the contract level, 21.5% of the 12,910 state contracts are paid by more than one channel (18.7% when each channel must pay at least 5%), and these contracts carry 47.0% of the paid value, because mixing is a feature of the large works: the loan and its counterpart, the Union transfer and the state's own money, the earmarked fund and the Treasury. At the work level, where a state identifies the work, between 0.4% and 100.0% of the works are mixed (Santa Catarina 21.9%, Goiás 31.4%, Minas Gerais 31.7%, Paraná's prototype 36.8%; Rio de Janeiro 5.3% and São Paulo 2.7% by the register, but every São Paulo work declared as IDB-financed is mixed). At the road level, between 17.1% and 75.0% of the state roads with contracts have more than one channel on them, and on the federal highways 40.2% of the 316 assets of the panel show two or more channels over the period (co-location, not the same contract). Mixing is therefore the rule for the works that matter and the exception for the routine contract.

2. What are the five main problems in the contracts?

Measured on every valid contract of the base, states and Union, each with its own denominator (a contract without the field stays out of the denominator and is never read as zero). The problems are ranked by the share of contracts affected; the reasons written in amendment texts are not in the ranking, because only one state publishes them (see the note after the list).

  1. The contract is extended beyond its original term states 49.8%, Union 50.4%States: state contracts with original and current term (SP, BA, SC, part of MG and RS) (n = 5,198). Union: federal contracts with planned and current end (n = 2,604). execution
  2. The contract value grows above the original value states 47.6%, Union 43.9%States: state contracts with original and current value (7 states) (n = 8,067). Union: federal contracts with initial and current value (n = 2,449). execution
  3. The contract is paid in a year of real fiscal cut (30% or more in the state's road payments) states 33.6%, Union n/aStates: state contracts with at least one payment year measured for cuts (10 states) (n = 12,002). Union: entity level: the Union's real road spending fell 40% in 2015 (Chart A7). 35.3% of the payment gaps start in a year of real cut. fiscal
  4. A large part of the payment is carried over to later years (restos a pagar above 25% of the paid value) states 11.8%, Union 36.1%States: all state contracts with payments (10 states) (n = 12,910). Union: federal contracts with paid and carry-over fields (n = 1,967). payment
  5. The contract is interrupted (states: a year without payment between the first and the last; Union: a recorded stoppage or days stalled; two different measures, not comparable across spheres) states 5.4%, Union 36.8%States: payment gap of a year or more, all 10 states (8.8% on credit-paid contracts, 4.3% on the others); stoppage recorded in 7.6% of the 3530 contracts of SP, SC and RJ (n = 12,828). Union: federal contracts with the days-stalled field; work unfinished in 4.6% of 3152; rescinded or cancelled 5.4% of 2586 in the DNIT register (n = 494). execution and financing

What the written reasons add, where they exist. Santa Catarina is the only register in the base that publishes the justification of each amendment (917 contracts): term-only extensions are cited in 58.0% of them, design changes in 45.1%, budget or financial reasons in 12.3%, price or rebalancing in 8.1%, weather in 8.4% and site or land in 4.7%. This is an illustration of what sits behind problems 1 and 2, not a measure for the base; Paraná's GMS texts (596 contracts of 2007-2013) are the only other source that could be read the same way.

3. Which investments reach the end? The successful cases, by channel and size

One funnel instead of one rate. Every ended contract starts at 100% and drops out at the first step it fails: an interruption (states: a year without payment; Union: not completed, halted or stalled), a rescission, an extension. The lines are the universe where all four steps can be measured (4,609 state contracts with term data in São Paulo, Bahia, Santa Catarina and part of Minas Gerais and Rio Grande do Sul; 2,234 federal contracts with planned and current end). The table adds all 10 states for the three steps they can measure (7,964 ended contracts). The rescission flag is observed in Minas Gerais and recorded as absent in Bahia, Santa Catarina, Rio de Janeiro and Pernambuco; Goiás, Rio Grande do Sul, São Paulo and most of Piauí have no status field, so step 3 removes almost nothing there.

The pattern is consistent with the rest of the page: interruptions and rescissions are rare events everywhere the registers can see them; the extension is the common event, and it is the large works, paid with credit or by the Union, that are extended. The Treasury-paid contract, mostly maintenance and services, ends within its term half of the time; the credit-paid work, a quarter of the time. Volume and channel are confounded, so the governance coding will have to hold size constant before reading a channel effect, and will have to treat the federal step 2 as a register gap (not completed is not the same as not finished) until the ObrasGov status is validated.

Beyond description: what the causal audit adds

The descriptive page stops at associations. A separate audit (Causal Audit of the Thesis Hypotheses, section 9) tests the channel inside the same contract and year: where a contract receives, in one year, a note paid from a loan and a note paid from the Treasury's regular source, the loan note is carried over to the next year 16.5 pp less in São Paulo (t 5.3, 127 contracts) and 36 pp less in Goiás with the commitment month held constant (t 3.0); pooled 22.6 pp, wild bootstrap by contract p = 0.001. The work, the contractor, the state and the year are the same by construction; only the source of the money differs. The governance code is composed on measured fields in the Governance Code Builder.

Method, limits and checks

Nothing is typed by hand. Every chart and table reads one CSV in dados/, built by script 44 from the thesis bases: the state database of 14 states (padrao_canais), the federal project base and Panel 1 (tese_dashboard), and the external-credit and macro module (credito_externo). The index of files, sources, periods and units is in metadata_descriptive_statistics.xlsx, one sheet per chart.

Stages are never added. Committed, settled, paid and disbursed stay in separate columns; where two layers use different stages (the Union's paid, the states' committed) the chart says so. Missing is not zero. A state-year absent from the base, a contract without an end date or a loan without an extension measure is left out of the denominator and counted as such.

Deflation. IPCA, December, 2025 prices, as in Panel 1. GDP from the IBGE national accounts. Exchange rates at signature for external loans.

Checks. 95 of 95 reconciliation tests pass, among them 29 spot checks on contracts drawn at random from the base and traced from the source register to the chart row (ids in dados/spot_checks.csv). The thesis base itself passed 35 of 35 integrity checks on 20 October 2026. The fixed colours were validated for adjacent pairs under normal and colour-deficient vision.

Open points carried into the metadata. Four states without a note-to-contract key; the pre-2015 grouping of the Union's earmarked sources in Panel 1 (P-056); rescission dates not recorded by any register; tender dates or years only in São Paulo, Minas Gerais and Rio Grande do Sul (the modality also in Bahia and on the 2025 notes of Santa Catarina); credit paid on contracts that name the loan in only 404 of 3,224 cases.
